label: Stop
gloss: end this record here; nothing after this step runs for it
why: Lanes rejoin. A record that goes down the YES lane of a condition comes back out and keeps running the steps after the condition, unless something ends it. A stop ends the record where it stands. At Beacon, a duplicate invoice is parked in the Exception Queue in the YES lane - but without a stop it rejoins and is also written to the Payment Batch, so the duplicate gets paid anyway.
cue: if a hold lane does not end with a stop, the held record still flows into whatever comes after the condition
task: INV-9 was already paid. It is held in the Exception Queue, but it still reaches the Payment Batch. End the duplicate in the YES lane so only INV-1 is paid.
notes: Stop goes at the end of the YES lane, after the Exception Queue write.
After a stop, nothing else runs for that record - the steps after the condition are skipped.
Other records (INV-1, NO lane) are not affected; they rejoin and are paid.
